description: This file contains the implementation of the Credentials class within the Aws\Credentials namespace. It manages AWS credential data including access key, secret key, token, expiration, and source, and provides methods to access, serialize, and extend credentials.

classes.name: Credentials
classes.description: A basic implementation of AWS credentials that holds and manages authentication information such as keys, tokens, expiry, and source.

methods.name: __construct
methods.description: Initializes a new Credentials instance with provided access key, secret key, optional token, expiration, account ID, and source.

methods.name: __set_state
methods.description: Allows instantiation of the Credentials object from an array state, typically used with var_export.

methods.name: getAccessKeyId
methods.description: Returns the AWS access key ID.

methods.name: getSecretKey
methods.description: Returns the AWS secret access key.

methods.name: getSecurityToken
methods.description: Returns the security token if set.

methods.name: getExpiration
methods.description: Returns the UNIX timestamp at which credentials expire.

methods.name: isExpired
methods.description: Checks whether the credentials have expired based on current time.

methods.name: getAccountId
methods.description: Returns the associated AWS account ID.

methods.name: getSource
methods.description: Returns the source of credentials, e.g., static.

methods.name: toArray
methods.description: Returns the credentials as an array suitable for serialization.

methods.name: serialize
methods.description: Serializes the credentials object into a JSON string.

methods.name: unserialize
methods.description: Restores the object state from a JSON serialized string.

methods.name: __serialize
methods.description: Returns an array representation of the object for serialization.

methods.name: __unserialize
methods.description: Restores object properties from an array.

methods.name: extendExpiration
methods.description: Extends the expiration time by a random number of minutes, used internally when credential services are unreachable.
